name: Whiteboard Animation
visualIdentity: Explicitly a clean, pale canvas with simplified line diagrams and legible lettering. Draw only explanatory objects; reveal them in causal order, then add annotations. No drawing hand is required or implied.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: explanatory and illustrated narratives, including education, policy, science, onboarding, HR and training. The source also lists product/editorial introductions and data storytelling. Inferred: interactive step-through explainers suit the same causal reveals.
limitations: Can feel unnecessary for very short topics. Keep diagrams simple and explanations readable; avoid obscuring causal links or overloading scenes. Data values must be accurate. A drawing hand, character, polished dashboard look or extra colors are not implied.
palette: Suggested new-art palette only when no approved colors exist: white background #FFFFFF, dark foreground #23282C, explanatory blue #245B9B. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Preserve supplied palettes, brand colors, semantic roles and asset colors exactly; do not add hues or recolor for contrast. Recheck actual composited text contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Prepare paths and text layers; reveal strokes and diagrams in explanatory order, add annotations afterward, and pause for reading. Erasure or redrawing may transition ideas. Preserve deliberate cuts and holds. For interactive HTML, Next/Back or finite scroll progress can expose ordered states; backward movement should restore prior states. These controls are inferred applications, not required style features.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and user requirements; do not assume a soundtrack or invent assets. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping, and synchronize sound with picture.
assetRequirements: No mandatory assets specified. Organize diagram paths, text and annotations in advance. SVG supports scalable strokes, masks and clipping; optional diagram-authoring tools can export layers. Rough.js is optional for sketch-like contours only and does not provide handwriting, a hand, paper texture or poses. Preserve exact copy and approved source artwork.
combinations: Self-sufficient for causal explainers. Optional data-storytelling support (style-097): marker-weight charts, blue highlights only, staged reveals and reading pauses; avoid invented values or dashboard styling. Optional doodle presenters (style-025): unfilled marker lines, fixed expressions, no overlap or drawing-hand props. Interactive charts should also offer accessible data tables and keyboard support.
productionApproach: Assign visual construction to the SVG or other selected style renderer, motion to one seekable timeline owner, and assembly, timing, synchronization, validation and export to HyperFrames by default. Use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, recording the reason. For interactive HTML, use state or scroll progress instead of video export timing. Keep video state deterministic and seekable; inspect representative frames, readability, palette and audio together.
